messages.subject: Discrete data converted to fractions
parts:
Hello all,

I'm doing some N-mixture Poisson modeling of bird abundance point-count data. I know these models are for discrete count data.

However, I have multiple sites with different numbers of point-count stations, so to compare abundance across sites, I have to divide the number of birds detected by the number of point-count stations. 
So, for Site Y, Species X abundance ends up being # of Species X/point-count station, which yields a fraction. For example, Species X = 1.57 birds at Site Y.

Here's my question: Does modeling fractions for abundance (pseudo-continuous data) mess up N-mixture Poisson modeling?
This could also be an issue with Chi-square GOF tests, which I think for these models should be for discrete data only too (Bolker 2007). 
I've been messing with models in R unmarked package and Royle Biometrics in PRESENCE.

Thanks to anyone who may have a thought on this.

Regards,

Matt B.

sent from my space station

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Discrete data converted to fractions
parts:
Dear Matt,

the Nmix model assumes discrete counts, so your basic data structure must be station by occasion, and the elements in that matrix must be your discrete counts.

If you want to compare "sites", where sites comprise multiple stations, you can treat sites as a factor (= categorical explanatory variable) and use likelihood ratio tests or AIC to find out whether sites differ in expected abundance lambda. You can also predict lambda for the levels of the site factor, to obtain an estimate of the mean expected abundance at each site.

Kind regards  --  Marc
